## About this page

*Only in the desktop app.*

Connects the WM Pass browser extension to this app, so the extension uses the vault already open here and you unlock once.

#### How it works

The extension works on its own too. Connected, it asks this app for the logins that match the page and fills the one you pick.

To connect, turn on **Let the extension connect** and choose **Set up browsers**. Then, in the extension, open Settings, Desktop app and choose **Connect**. Both show a six-digit code; if they match, say so on both.

The browser starts a small relay program that carries sealed messages between the two. It holds no keys and cannot read them.

See also [Connecting the extension](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-bridge), [Let the extension connect](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-enabled).

<a id="setting-bridge-enabled"></a>

## Let the extension connect

*Only in the desktop app.*

Lets a connected browser extension ask this app for the logins that match the page you are on, and fill one.

#### How it works

WM Pass listens on a local socket on this computer. Any program could connect to it, so everything through it runs inside an encrypted session, and a new extension is accepted only after you compare a code on both screens.

An extension can ask whether the vault is open, ask for the items that match a page, fill one of those, and lock the vault. The list it sees has names and sites, never passwords or notes, and a fill for an item that does not match the page is refused.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Connected extensions can reach the vault open here. |
| Off | No extension can reach this app. The extension still works with its own vault. |

#### Limits

It does not protect against code running as the extension itself. A copied browser profile cannot connect, because the extension's key is sealed by the browser.

See also [Ask before the first fill on each site](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-ask-every-site), [Set up browsers](/guide/settings/browser/#action-setup-browsers), [Connecting the extension](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-bridge).

<a id="setting-bridge-ask-every-site"></a>

## Ask before the first fill on each site

*Only in the desktop app.*

The first time an extension fills a login on a site, WM Pass asks in a window of its own whether to allow it.

#### Why it is there

A web page cannot draw over this app's window or answer it for you, so a page cannot trick you into filling a login somewhere new.

#### How it works

Choosing **Fill** remembers the site for that extension, and it fills there without asking again. A site counts as its whole domain, so www.example.com and login.example.com are one site.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Each new site waits for your answer in this app. |
| Off | A connected extension fills any matching login without a question from this app. |

#### Limits

A settings file cannot turn this off. Forgetting an extension also forgets the sites you approved for it.

See also [Let the extension connect](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-enabled), [Connected extensions](/guide/settings/browser/#group-browser-paired).

<a id="action-setup-browsers"></a>

## Set up browsers

*Only in the desktop app.*

Tells each browser on this computer where the relay program is, so the extension can start it.

#### How it works

For each browser it finds, WM Pass writes a small file naming the relay program and the WM Pass extension, the only one allowed to start it. It looks for Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi and Firefox. On Windows it also adds a registry entry for each.

#### Limits

A browser is found by its profile folder, so one you have never opened is skipped. Run this again after you install another browser.

See also [Let the extension connect](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-enabled), [Browser extension](/guide/settings/browser/).

<a id="action-bridge-fingerprint"></a>

## Fingerprint

*Only in the desktop app.*

A short form of the key this app uses for the extension link.

#### How it works

A connected extension remembers this key. If something answers in this app's place with a different key, the extension refuses it.

#### Limits

If this app ever makes a new key, such as on a fresh install, extensions that connected before refuse it.

See also [Let the extension connect](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-enabled), [Connected extensions](/guide/settings/browser/#group-browser-paired).

<a id="group-browser-paired"></a>

## Connected extensions

*Only in the desktop app.*

The extensions that have compared a code with this app and may connect.

#### How it works

Each shows the browser it says it runs in. The remove button beside one forgets it at once, ends any connection it has open, and drops the sites you approved for it. To connect again, it has to compare a code again.

#### Limits

The name is only what the extension says about itself. The code you compared is what proves it.

See also [Let the extension connect](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-enabled), [Ask before the first fill on each site](/guide/settings/browser/#setting-bridge-ask-every-site).
